categories.main_business_segments: Bank of Communications primarily operates in four main business segments: corporate banking, retail banking, treasury operations, and other financial services. Corporate banking includes loans, trade finance, and deposits for corporate clients. Retail banking covers personal loans, deposits, credit cards, wealth management, and private banking. Treasury operations involve money market activities, bond investments, and foreign exchange services. The bank also has subsidiaries engaged in financial leasing, fund management, trust, insurance, and overseas securities businesses.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The bank emphasizes digital transformation and financial technology integration, including mobile banking platforms for individuals and enterprises, online banking, and AI-driven customer service and risk management. It has developed enterprise-level architecture, business middle platforms, and product factories to enhance digital operations. The bank also employs advanced risk measurement models, credit risk assessment tools, and financial asset valuation techniques including fair value measurement and impairment models aligned with accounting standards.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The bank serves a broad customer base including 2.62 million corporate clients and 192 million retail customers. Key markets include small and micro enterprises, strategic emerging industries, manufacturing, green finance sectors, and rural/agricultural clients. It supports national strategies such as rural revitalization, green development, and technological innovation. Geographically, it serves customers across China’s major economic regions and internationally through its overseas branches.
categories.geographic_coverage: The bank operates extensively across China with over 2,800 domestic branches covering all major regions including the Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta, Bohai Rim, Central, Western, and Northeast China. It maintains 23 overseas branches and representative offices in global financial centers such as Hong Kong, New York, London, Singapore, Tokyo, Frankfurt, and others, with 69 overseas outlets in total. It actively supports cross-border trade and RMB internationalization.
categories.supply_chain_position: As a large state-owned commercial bank, Bank of Communications operates primarily in the midstream and downstream of the financial supply chain, providing financing, deposit, payment, and wealth management services. It acts as a financial intermediary between depositors and borrowers, supports trade finance and supply chain finance, and offers investment and asset management products. Its subsidiaries extend services into upstream financial leasing and trust sectors.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The bank’s strategic focus is on building a world-class bank group with distinctive advantages, emphasizing green finance as a core theme. It prioritizes four business features: inclusive finance, trade finance, technology finance, and wealth finance. Digital transformation and Shanghai as a strategic hub are key breakthrough points. The bank invests heavily in fintech innovation, AI applications, data governance, and risk management digitalization. It also focuses on supporting national strategies like carbon neutrality, rural revitalization, and technological self-reliance.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated mainly through net interest income from loans and deposits, fee and commission income from banking services such as card services, wealth management, custody, and investment banking. The bank also earns investment income from securities and equity investments, and income from leasing and insurance subsidiaries. It maintains a diversified income structure with a growing proportion of non-interest income.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Bank of Communications is one of China’s major state-owned commercial banks and ranks 9th globally by Tier 1 capital among banks. It is recognized as a global systemically important bank. Its main competitors include other large Chinese banks such as Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, China Construction Bank, Agricultural Bank of China, and Bank of China. The bank positions itself as a stable, innovative, and customer-centric institution with strong capabilities in digital finance and green banking.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of end 2023, the bank’s total assets reached RMB 14.06 trillion, an 8.23% increase year-on-year. Customer loans grew 9.08% to RMB 7.96 trillion, and customer deposits increased 7.58% to RMB 8.55 trillion. Net profit attributable to shareholders was RMB 92.73 billion, up 0.68%. The bank maintains strong capital adequacy ratios with a capital adequacy ratio of 15.27% and a core Tier 1 ratio of 10.23%. It has a stable and growing financial profile with improving asset quality and risk coverage.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The bank emphasizes its role as a state-owned large bank supporting the real economy and financial stability. It differentiates through its comprehensive financial services covering corporate, retail, wealth, and green finance. Its digital transformation initiatives provide convenient, intelligent, and scenario-based financial services. The bank’s strong presence in Shanghai and international markets, combined with its focus on innovation, risk management, and ESG integration, offers customers reliable, diversified, and sustainable financial solutions.
